stemMarkdown: Find the difference (in Rs.) between the compound interest and the simple interest on Rs. 29000 at 10% per annum for 2 years. (Round to 2 decimal places.)
solutionMarkdown: CI: the amount after 2 years is $35090.00$, so CI $= 6090.00$. SI $= \dfrac{29000 \times 10 \times 2}{100} = 5800.00$. The difference is $290.0$.
altSolutionMarkdown: For 2 years the gap is always the interest earned on the first year's interest: $P\left(\dfrac{R}{100}\right)^2 = 29000 \times \left(\dfrac{10}{100}\right)^2 = 290.0$.
